about: The intent ledger: what the protocol is FOR, stated as checkable intentions, each linked to the spec sections and decisions meant to deliver it. build_dashboard.py joins every check from conformance/*/out/summary.json to an intent when they share a spec section or decision. An intent can fail while every clause passes; that gap is what this file exists to show. Sources are quoted so Venkat can correct the reading.

intents.title: A fork can be compared with its source
intents.quote: A fork allows you to do whatever you want to the imported text, which is why it needs a pinned version to point to, so a reader can compare the mod to the source. For example if I tactically edit your original to misrepresent you, the pin ground-truths it.
intents.suspected_gap: Decision #57 (§16.6f, gate G11; built in blygger-studio 0.20.0) fixes the quote half: a fork of a thread now flattens the pinned document's baked quotes, so a fork no longer re-quotes at the forker's versions. Still open: no rule requires the fork's public page to show its lineage or link the pinned source. Live data has 4 of 5 fork pages doing it and Brady Dale's not doing it.

intents.title: A quote is verifiably part of its source
intents.quote: It verifies that the quoted bit is actually part of the transcluded item and you're not making shit up.
intents.suspected_gap: Verifiable only while the origin still serves the quoted version (live or pinned). After the source is republished and that version was never pinned, the check can no longer run.

intents.title: Forks are chain-of-custody trails
intents.quote: Forks are chain of custody trails when you want to proceed through transformations.
intents.suspected_gap: #57 makes a fork descend from the pinned bytes, and flattened quotes keep a 'quoted from' line. Those quotes are now in the plain-web register (editable, unverified), so the chain of custody runs only through forked_from back to the pin, one hop at a time. Is one hop per fork the intended chain?

intents.title: A trustworthy ground-truth content graph that AI and humans can both use
intents.quote: The whole idea is to create a hardened ground truth content graph that can use AI and human creativity freely while remaining trustworthy.
intents.suspected_gap: Provenance is self-asserted by design (#20). 'Hardened' therefore means 'inspectable', not 'verified'. Worth making sure that is the intended meaning.

intents.title: Unpinned history is never exposed
intents.quote: No route serves unpinned history in any representation, and a version display MUST NOT offer, imply, or hint at access to unpinned versions.

intents.title: Withdrawal rolls to null everywhere except pins
intents.quote: Readers may retain exactly what the origin still serves (pinned versions) and MUST roll everything else to null.
intents.suspected_gap: Thread snapshots are deliberately independent of source withdrawal (#9, §10.4), so the withdrawn text survives inside other people's threads. Is that the intended exception?

intents.title: The state plane is ground truth; the feed is only a signal
intents.quote: The archive index is the reconciliation surface; the feed is a cheap trigger. Gaps, skew, and malformed feeds degrade to an index diff, never to loss.

intents.title: A reader's version watermark never silently goes backwards
intents.quote: The local version watermark never silently regresses. A lower-than-watermark version is surfaced as a suspected history rewrite.

intents.title: If you are quoted, stubbed or forked, you can find out, verifiably
intents.quote: An origin that has been quoted, stubbed, or forked can find out, reliably and verifiably, without subscribing to the quoter.
intents.suspected_gap: Webmention is optional at L2, so an origin that doesn't advertise an endpoint never learns it was responded to. 'Can find out' holds only for origins that opted in.

intents.title: Every feed works in a plain RSS reader, with self-contained HTML
intents.quote: Every blyg feed is a valid RSS 2.0 feed whose items carry self-contained HTML.

intents.title: A mirror can't take on another origin's identity
intents.quote: Subscription identity = final fetch origin, never the manifest's self-asserted site. A mirror must not inherit another origin's identity.

intents.title: Publishing never depends on the network
intents.quote: The local snapshot is what gets baked, never a live fetch: publish does not depend on the network, quoting follows reading.
intents.suspected_gap: A fork's publish SHOULD check the pin with one fetch (§5.6 r2). That is softened to warn-on-network-failure, so it is consistent, but it is the one place publishing touches the network.

intents.title: Long-form threads, pins and forks, not just a short-post feed
intents.quote: There's a lot more social stubbing than I expected and less forking, and not much threading with transcludes yet... Strong synchronic bias. I need to amp up the diachronic. Pins, threads, and forks are going to be the next focus.
intents.suspected_gap: A usage intent, not a protocol one. The live crawler's census of item kinds and references measures it directly.
